$comment: Per-title OVERRIDES only. This is deliberately not a list of games.
Steam titles need no entry here. The backend discovers them by reading
steamapps/libraryfolders.vdf and each library's appmanifest_<appid>.acf (29 installed apps
across 3 libraries on the reference host). At launch it reads Steam's local appinfo.vdf,
prefers the compatible Windows VR entry, and starts its executable directly with the declared
arguments, working directory, SteamAppId and SteamGameId. This avoids steam:// confirmation
dialogs while retaining Steam ownership and API context.
WHY THERE IS NO LONGER A PER-TITLE 'chain'. An earlier version of this file gave every title a
runtime chain, because the broker had claimed CloudXR as the machine-wide 64-bit OpenXR runtime
and so every game had to redirect itself to VDXR with per-launch environment variables. That is
inverted as of 2026-07-27: the machine default is VDXR (as it is under Virtual Desktop, which is
why VD needs no per-game setup) and the BROKER carries the explicit override to CloudXR. One
process we control, rather than every game forever. Games now launch with no environment at all.
Verified both directions simultaneously: an app with no override reports
'VirtualDesktopXR (Standalone)', while the broker still reports CloudXR and still receives PQW
foveation data (a CloudXR-only extension).
CONSEQUENCE TO BE AWARE OF. Launching through Steam means we cannot inject per-game environment
variables, so VISIONVNC_CB_LAYER_DISABLE can no longer be set per title and our API layer is
always active. That is what gaze-driven foveation needs, but the ovrshim titles previously used
that flag to avoid controller double-injection. The replacement must be a registry setting
(HKCU\Software\VisionVNC\ControllerBridge already exists for calibration), not an env var.

$overrideSchema.steamAppId: match a discovered Steam title by app id
$overrideSchema.name: display name override, if the Steam manifest name is unhelpful
$overrideSchema.notes: shown in the gallery as a caveat
$overrideSchema.launchOptionsHint: what to paste into Steam's own launch options; we do not set these

steamOverrides.notes: Reduce in-game graphics quality rather than resolution when testing. VisionVNC's optimized profile launches Alyx directly with its measured fidelity and MSAA arguments.
Steam metadata has a separate Windows VR entry, Hyperbolica.exe startXR. VisionVNC selects it automatically instead of the desktop-default entry.
SteamVR is a runtime, not streamable content. CloudXR 6.2 has no SteamVR headset driver; OpenVR titles use OpenComposite instead.
Steamworks Common Redistributables is a shared prerequisite, not streamable content.
32-bit OpenVR via the mod's own launcher; relies on the WOW6432Node ActiveRuntime pointing at VDXR-32. Launch from Steam normally.

nonSteamTitles.name: hello_xr (diagnostic)
notes: NOTHING READS THIS FILE. The launcher's list is the backend's discovered Steam titles plus
hand-added custom ones (GameLibrary's state file); this entry documents intent and does not
create a tile. hello_xr was added to the reference host as a custom title on 2026-07-28
(GamesAddCustom -> custom:f049dff7a5d7, exposed) so it can be launched from the headset as a
cheap content app for checking the wrist HUD before a real title.
Two distinct uses, do not confuse them. As a CONTENT app (what the gallery launches) it takes
VDXR like any game and renders through the broker — no environment, nothing special. As a
SUBSTITUTE for the broker as the CloudXR application it needs XR_RUNTIME_JSON pointed at
CloudXR explicitly and must not run alongside a live broker; that is the VisionVNC-HelloXR
scheduled task, and it is the control that exonerated the broker during the pivot-dropout
